In [[number theory]], an '''evil number''' is a non-negative integer that has an even [[Hamming weight|number of 1s]] in its [[Binary number|binary expansion]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite OEIS|A001969|name=Evil numbers: numbers with an even number of 1's in their binary expansion|mode=cs2}}</ref> These numbers give the positions of the zero values in the [[Thue–Morse sequence]], and for this reason they have also been called the '''Thue–Morse set'''.<ref>{{citation|last1=Charlier|first1=Émilie|last2=Cisternino|first2=Célia|last3=Massuir|first3=Adeline|contribution=State complexity of the multiples of the Thue-Morse set|doi=10.4204/EPTCS.305.3|mr=4030092|pages=34–49|series=Electron. Proc. Theor. Comput. Sci. (EPTCS)|title=Proceedings Tenth International Symposium on Games, Automata, Logics, and Formal Verification|volume=305|year=2019|doi-access=free|arxiv=1903.06114}}</ref> Non-negative integers that are not evil are called [[odious number]]s.

==Examples==
The first evil numbers are 0, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12, 15, 17, 18, 20, 23, 24, 27, 29, 30, 33, 34, 36, 39, and so on.<ref name=":0" />

==Equal sums==
The partition of the non-negative integers into the odious and evil numbers is the unique partition of these numbers into two sets that have equal [[multiset]]s of pairwise sums.<ref>{{citation|last1=Lambek|first1=J.|author1-link=Joachim Lambek|last2=Moser|first2=L.|author2-link=Leo Moser|doi=10.4153/CMB-1959-013-x|journal=[[Canadian Mathematical Bulletin]]|mr=104631|pages=85–89|title=On some two way classifications of integers|volume=2|year=1959|issue=2 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

As 19th-century mathematician Eugène Prouhet showed, the partition into evil and odious numbers of the numbers from <math>0</math> to <math>2^k-1</math>, for any <math>k</math>, provides a solution to the [[Prouhet–Tarry–Escott problem]] of finding sets of numbers whose sums of powers are equal up to the <math>k</math>th power.<ref>{{citation|last=Wright|first=E. M.|doi=10.2307/2309513|journal=American Mathematical Monthly|mr=104622|pages=199–201|title=Prouhet's 1851 solution of the Tarry-Escott problem of 1910|volume=66|year=1959|issue=3 |jstor=2309513 }}</ref>

==In computer science==
In [[computer science]], an evil number is said to have [[Parity bit#Parity|even parity]].
